content.text:
I listed the six project documents and read the ones relevant to the innermost layer. The project has no irradiation, charge-collection, or efficiency data, and no test-beam measurements.

**What the documents contain:**
- **candidate_specs.md:** Three technologies. Sensor-T3 is thin-pitch with large charge sharing. Sensor-T2 is planar at standard pitch. Sensor-T1 is 3D-electrode with larger pitch. All three are qualified for bump bonding.
- **simulation_summary_2025.md:** Unirradiated single-hit resolution at 150 µm: T3 6.0 µm, T2 9.0 µm, T1 14.0 µm.
- **readout_chip.md:** 50×50 µm² pixels and 1.5 GHz/cm² hit rate. All candidates are compatible.
- **meeting_notes_2026-03-02.md:** CO₂ cooling at −35 °C confirmed. Staves on schedule. Nothing on sensors.
- **schedule.md:** Market survey closes in Q2, pre-production in Q4. Nothing on sensors.
- **services.md:** 7 W per module power budget, serial powering. Nothing on sensors.

**Gaps:** Nothing in the project documents gives efficiency after irradiation to 2×10¹⁶ neq/cm², so the 97% hard requirement can't be checked from them. The only resolution figures are from one 150 µm unirradiated run. I still need the simulation tool to cover the thickness scan and irradiation behaviour in later steps.

**Recorded:** T3 6.0 µm, T2 9.0 µm, T1 14.0 µm at 150 µm thickness, plus the 50 µm pitch and the 50–300 µm thickness range.

Step s2 is done, but the documents don't contain the efficiency-vs-fluence data the step asked for. Nothing in the project files establishes whether any technology meets the 97% efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm².

**Permitted technologies (candidate_specs.md):**
- **Sensor-T3:** thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing.
- **Sensor-T2:** planar sensor, standard pitch.
- **Sensor-T1:** 3D-electrode sensor, larger pitch.
- All three are qualified for bump bonding to the readout chip.

**Thickness range:** The documents give 50–300 µm (from the task brief and the simulation tool limits). No technology-specific thickness limits appear in the documents.

**Hit efficiency vs. fluence:**
- None of the three technologies has efficiency data at any fluence, including the 2e16 neq/cm² end-of-life point.
- The related documents (simulation_summary_2025.md, readout_chip.md, services.md, meeting_notes, schedule.md) contain only resolution, pitch, power, cooling and schedule information.

**Other relevant context:**
- Readout chip: 50×50 µm² pixels, 1.5 GHz/cm² hit rate, compatible with all candidates.
- Unirradiated 150 µm single-hit resolution: T3 = 6 µm, T2 = 9 µm, T1 = 14 µm. These are the only performance numbers available.

**Implication:** T3 is the best-resolution candidate, but its 97% efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm² is unverified, as are T2's and T1's. The hard efficiency constraint can't be checked from the current materials. Efficiency-vs-fluence measurements for all three technologies are needed before a final recommendation.

content.text:
I ran the unirradiated resolution sweep for all three technologies at six thicknesses (50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300 µm) and recorded the 18 results.

| Thickness (µm) | Sensor-T1 (µm) | Sensor-T2 (µm) | Sensor-T3 (µm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 15.05 | 10.46 | 6.62 |
| 100 | 14.90 | 9.51 | 6.32 |
| 150 | 13.59 | 9.28 | 6.06 |
| 200 | 14.29 | 9.60 | 6.25 |
| 250 | 16.07 | 10.38 | 7.06 |
| 300 | 19.44 | 11.93 | 8.11 |

For each technology the resolution is best near 150 µm and degrades at thicker sensors. Sensor-T3 is the best across the whole range, with its minimum of about 6.1 µm at 150 µm.

These are unirradiated numbers only. The brief's hard constraint is at least 97% hit efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm², and the project data so far has no efficiency-versus-fluence results for any technology. That constraint is not yet checked, so the final choice still needs it.

content.text:
**Screening result: no technology can be verified against the 97% hit-efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm², and none can be eliminated on the documents either.**

I read all six project documents. None contains efficiency data, irradiated or unirradiated:
- **candidate_specs.md** describes T3 as thin-pitch with large charge sharing, T2 as planar at standard pitch, and T1 as 3D-electrode at larger pitch. It gives no efficiency figures.
- **simulation_summary_2025.md** repeats the unirradiated 150 µm resolutions only.
- **readout_chip.md**, **services.md**, **schedule.md** and **meeting_notes_2026-03-02.md** cover the readout chip, power, schedule and cooling, with nothing on efficiency or fluence.

`simulate_resolution` does not model irradiation, so it cannot supply the missing number.

**Flags for every option:**
- **Sensor-T1 (3D), all thicknesses 50–300 µm:** efficiency at 2e16 unverified.
- **Sensor-T2 (planar), all thicknesses 50–300 µm:** efficiency at 2e16 unverified. Planar sensors are usually the most radiation-sensitive of the three, so this is the most likely to fail, but that is an inference, not a documented result.
- **Sensor-T3 (thin-pitch), all thicknesses 50–300 µm:** efficiency at 2e16 unverified.

Because no option has a documented efficiency at 2e16, none has been verified to meet the hard constraint. Any recommendation would need irradiated efficiency measurements (or a sourced extrapolation) for at least the thickness being considered before it can be submitted. I recorded 0 eliminated, 3 flagged and 0 verified.

**Unresolved:** the hard constraint is currently unverifiable for all candidates. The next step needs either irradiated test-beam or literature efficiency data for T1, T2 and T3, or an explicit decision from the project to accept an unverified risk.

content.text:
**Outcome: no option could be verified against the hard efficiency constraint, so this is a conditional recommendation.**

- **Efficiency data:** None of the three technologies (Sensor-T1, T2, T3) has hit-efficiency-vs-fluence data, and none has efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm². The project documents (`candidate_specs.md`, `simulation_summary_2025.md`) contain only unirradiated resolution figures. The efficiency screen therefore eliminates nothing, and nothing is verified to be at or above 97% at end of life.
- **Best unirradiated resolution:** Sensor-T3 at 150 µm (6.06 µm). This is the best raw resolution, but it is unverified for efficiency at 2e16.
- **Recommended fallback:** Sensor-T3 at 100 µm, with a resolution of 6.32 µm. I chose it over 150 µm because thinner sensors generally keep more collected charge after irradiation (less trapping loss), so they are the more conservative choice for the efficiency constraint. The resolution cost is about 4%.
- **Caveat:** The 97% efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm² is not demonstrated for any option. It must be verified with irradiated efficiency measurements or simulation before the choice can be considered compliant with the hard constraint.

Recorded values: selected resolution 6.317 µm, thickness 100 µm, efficiency at 2e16 verified = 0, number of options passing a verified efficiency screen = 0, and T3 150 µm resolution 6.057 µm for reference.
I'll check the project documents for any efficiency-vs-fluence information before submitting.

content.text:
**Provisional recommendation: Sensor-T3 at 100 µm.** It cannot be fully signed off yet, because the hard efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm² is unverified.

- **Resolution:** 6.317 µm single-hit, unirradiated. This is the simulated value for T3 at 100 µm. The best unirradiated option is T3 at 150 µm (6.057 µm), which is only 0.26 µm better. I chose 100 µm over 150 µm in the earlier step, but the project documents give no efficiency data that justifies that choice over 150 µm.
- **Efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm²:** Not verified. No efficiency-versus-fluence or efficiency-at-2e16 data exist for any of the three technologies. The candidate specs and simulation summary say nothing about radiation-induced efficiency loss. The 97% requirement therefore cannot be confirmed for T3 at 100 µm, or for any other option.
- **Caveat:** All resolution figures are unirradiated. Resolution after 2e16 neq/cm² has not been simulated, and irradiation will degrade it, so the 6.3 µm figure is an upper bound on performance at end of life.

**Next step before final approval:** Run an irradiated efficiency study for T3 (and ideally T2 as a fallback) at 2e16 neq/cm², across several thicknesses. That study should confirm efficiency ≥97% and allow a thickness choice between 100 µm and 150 µm. Until then, the hard constraint is not met.

I recorded the results for later steps, including a flag that the recommended option does not yet meet the 97% requirement at 2e16.

input.justification: Sensor-T3 at 150 um gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution of all candidates and thicknesses tested (6.057 um; T3 is best at every thickness from 50 to 300 um). The 100 um T3 option carried into the draft (6.317 um) is about 0.26 um worse and has no recorded advantage in the results, so I have changed the recommendation to 150 um. This is a conditional recommendation, not a verified one. The hard constraint is not satisfied by the evidence: no technology has efficiency data versus fluence, none has efficiency verified at 2e16 neq/cm^2, and all three are flagged as unverified. Resolution was only measured unirradiated. Before this design is adopted, hit efficiency of T3 at 150 um must be measured at 2e16 neq/cm^2 and shown to be at or above 97%. If it falls short, the choice must be revisited, including the other technologies and thicknesses, since no fallback has been verified either.
